Tables of the open data service

Source: R/odat.R
odtab.Rd

odls() lists the tables of the project's open data service and odtab() loads one by its key, as the service serves it at the time of the call. Everything about a table (its address, rows, columns and SHA-256) is read from the service's manifest at run time, so a table that its publisher has replaced is loaded as it is now, with no new release of crimlab.

Usage

odtab(
  key,
  cols = NULL,
  refresh = FALSE,
  base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev")
)

odls(base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev"))

Arguments

key

A table's key, as odls() lists it.

cols

The names of the columns to keep, or NULL (all).

refresh

TRUE downloads the table again even when the cache holds a copy that matches.

base

The address of the service, or of a mirror of it (a folder holding manifest.json and <db>/<table>.csv.gz, which may be a file:// address). The default is getOption("crimlab.data"), or the project's service when that is not set.

Value

odls() a data frame with a row per table: key, rows, bytes (of the gzip file), sha256 (NA for a table that cannot be checked) and columns, a list of the column names. odtab() the table as a data frame.

Details

A downloaded file is used only when its SHA-256 is the one the manifest lists. When it is not, the manifest is read once more (the table may have been replaced between the two requests) and, if the file still does not match, it is deleted and odtab() stops. A table the manifest lists without a SHA-256 cannot be checked and is not loaded.

Tables are kept in tools::R_user_dir("crimlab", "cache"). A kept file is used again only while its SHA-256 is the one the manifest lists now; otherwise, or with refresh = TRUE, the table is downloaded again.

The file is read as CSV (RFC 4180): fields separated by commas, a field in double quotes may hold commas, line breaks and doubled quotes, lines end in LF or CRLF, a byte order mark is skipped. A blank line is a row of a table of one column (its value missing), and is skipped in a wider table, as read.csv() skips it. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are kept as text, each written <xx> (its value in hexadecimal), so no value is lost and none is in an invalid encoding.

The columns are those of the file, named as served (an empty or a repeated name too). cols picks some of them, matched without regard to case or underscores ("case_id" finds "CaseID"), so that a publisher's respelling of a name does not break a call; an exact name is preferred.

The values are those the file holds. Every column is read as text; an empty field and the text NA are missing values. A column becomes numbers only when every value in it is a plain decimal number that a number holds exactly as written: digits with at most a leading minus, a decimal point and an exponent, no leading zero, at most 15 significant digits, and not so large or so small that a number cannot hold it ("1e400", "1e-400" and "1e-320" stay text). So identifiers such as "007" (not the same as "7"), long identifiers, dates and codes such as "F" stay text, and no column becomes logical. A column of whole numbers within R's integer range is integer, any other numeric column double.

Errors: a key the manifest does not list; a table listed without a SHA-256; a file that does not match it; a line with more or fewer fields than the header, a quote inside a field that is not in quotes, a quoted field never closed, text after a closing quote or a NUL byte (each naming the line); a table whose number of rows is not the one the manifest lists; a column the table does not have, or a name that matches more than one; a service that cannot be reached, answers with an error or does not answer in time (60 seconds for the manifest, 600 for a table, or getOption("timeout") if longer).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the internet
tabs <- odls()
head(tabs[, c("key", "rows")])
x <- odtab(tabs$key[!is.na(tabs$sha256)][1L])
str(x)
} # }
